events.name: Safari Zone
events.intro: A long fence of split rails, and behind it grass up to a person's shoulder, moving in a wind you can't feel. A warden in a wide hat stands at the gate with a ledger. Mrs. Okoye, the warden: "Rare Pokémon inside. Five hundred to enter. No battles in there, not one. Mind your steps: you get thirty, and every one counts."

success.text: She takes the money and writes your name in the ledger in neat round letters. "Thirty steps. Bait makes them linger; rocks make them easier to catch, and quicker to bolt. I show you the odds. I always show the odds."

"No battles: we don't hurt them here. Thirty steps; bait costs you five, creeping up slow costs ten. Throw bait and they stay longer. Throw a rock and they're easier, but they're more likely to run. Every throw, I tell you the odds first. Fair?" It is.
You thank her and walk on along the fence. Something enormous moves in the grass on the other side, keeping pace with you a while.

events.name: Safari Ticket
events.intro: A warden at the fence holds up a stiff paper ticket and waves you over. "Somebody left a day pass at the gate. Take it." Behind you a small girl is pressed against the rails, staring at the grass the way you stare at a shop window.

success.text: "Free entry, then. Thirty steps, same as everyone." She tears the stub and lets you through.

choices.label: Give it to the kid behind me.

success.text: The girl looks at the ticket, then at you, then runs in before anyone can change their mind. Half an hour later she comes back out with a Nidoran♀ in her arms and her whole face shining, and she shows you, and shows you again.

effects.text: You gave your Safari pass to a little girl, and she caught her first Pokémon.

events.name: Safari Zone
events.intro: The gate swings shut behind you. Grass, and sky, and the smell of warm earth. Mrs. Okoye calls through the rails: "Thirty steps. No battles. I'll be at the far gate."

success.text: You step into the grass. You count your first step without meaning to.

branches.text: You step into the grass. "Five extra steps," Mrs. Okoye calls, "for the one you let go last time."

success.text: You turn back at the gate. Mrs. Okoye nods: some days are for looking.

events.name: Safari Zone
events.intro: The Grassland. Something stirs in the tall grass: a herd of Doduo racing in circles, heads bobbing, all three of each head talking at once.

success.text: You toss the bait wide. The herd slows, and circles it, and starts to peck. They are not going anywhere now.
The Ball wobbles once, twice, three times. Click. A Doduo, all three heads indignant.

failure.text: The Doduo bursts out and the whole herd scatters, shrieking, in nine directions at once.

success.text: You let the herd race on and walk deeper in.

remembers.notice: The herd is busy at the bait, slow and careless.

addChoices.label: Throw a Ball at the feeding herd.

success.text: They barely look up. The Ball clicks shut on a Doduo with its mouth still full.

failure.text: It pops out, still chewing, and trots off after the others.

events.name: Safari Zone: rare
events.intro: The Rare Cry. An unusual cry from beyond a hedge of reeds: high and sweet, nothing like the herds. Through the reeds you can see it: a Chansey, or a Dratini in a pond, or a Tauros standing alone, depending on where the wind is.

success.text: You creep forward a step at a time, ten steps that take an age. It hears you, and looks, and does not run. You are close now.
The rock lands short, and it flinches, and in that instant your Ball is already in the air. It holds. It is yours.

effects.text: You caught something rare in the Safari Zone.

failure.text: It startles at the rock and is gone, a cry fading into the grass. You stand there with the Ball in your hand.

success.text: You leave it to its reeds. Some things you are glad just to have seen.

remembers.notice: It is watching you, close enough to touch.

success.text: You roll the Ball the last little way. It sniffs it, and lets it take it. A rare catch, and a gentle one.

effects.text: You caught something rare in the Safari Zone, gently.

failure.text: At the last moment it bolts. Close. So close.

events.name: Safari Zone: wild
events.intro: The Wild Patch. Something stirs: a Kangaskhan with a baby in her pouch, watching you over the top of a thornbush. The baby peeks out, and ducks, and peeks out again.

success.text: You stay where you are and keep your hands down. The mother watches. Then the baby climbs half out of the pouch and waves at you with its whole arm. Your team waves back.
You lay the bait down and back away. The mother comes for it, slowly, and lets you stay near while she eats.
Somehow it holds. You open your eyes. The mother looks at the Ball, and at you, and does not seem to mind at all.

failure.text: She bats the Ball back to you, quite gently. The baby laughs.

remembers.notice: She lets you near while she eats.

success.text: So close you could touch her. The Ball clicks. She doesn't seem to mind; the baby, inside with her, waves through the glass.

failure.text: She shrugs the Ball off and goes back to eating. No hard feelings.

events.name: Safari Zone: exit
events.intro: The Exit. Daylight over the far gate. Mrs. Okoye is waiting with her ledger open. "Steps all used? Show me what you found."

success.text: She looks at each one properly, writes it in her ledger, and nods. "Well caught. Well treated." She hands you a few Balls for the road.
You open a Ball at the gate and let the one you caught last go back into the grass. It looks back once. Mrs. Okoye smiles, a slow wide smile. "Next time, five more steps. On me."

events.name: Battle Frontier
events.intro: A building like a cathedral, all glass and white stone, with the sound of a crowd somewhere inside. A clerk in a pressed jacket checks your name off a list. Mr. Diallo, the Frontier clerk: "Four rounds, one arena. Win four or lose one. Your Pokémon are healed between rounds. No items in battle. No mercy, no shame."

success.text: He opens the arena doors. The noise of the crowd hits you like weather.
"No shame," says Mr. Diallo, and means it.

Mr. Diallo turns the list round so you can read it. Round one leads with a Fighting-type. Round two, a veteran's old Normal-type. Round three, twins, two at once. Round four: the Brain, and next to her name, only a question mark.

events.name: Battle Frontier
events.intro: Round 1. Your first opponent bounces on her toes at the far end of the arena. Ace Trainer Corinne: "First round's always nerves. Mine, not yours."

success.text: "Okay. Okay okay okay. Let's go."

remembers.notice: Second time through: they have heard about you, and they have trained.

success.text: "Okay. Okay okay okay. Let's go."

events.name: Battle Frontier: trainer
events.intro: Round 2. An old man in a frayed cap, his Pokémon as grey at the muzzle as he is. Veteran Hask: "I've lost here forty times. This is forty-one, or my first win."

success.text: He nods, and sets his feet.
He laughs, surprised into it. "You too. Mean it."

win.text: Veteran Hask lost his forty-first Frontier battle to you, and shook your hand.

remembers.notice: Second time through: they have heard about you, and they have trained.

success.text: He nods, and sets his feet.

events.name: Battle Frontier: trainer
events.intro: Round 3. Two girls in matching scarves, finishing each other's sentences. The Twins, Sib and Sab: "Doubles!" "DOUBLES!"

success.text: They point at you at exactly the same moment.

remembers.notice: Second time through: they have heard about you, and they have trained.

success.text: They point at you at exactly the same moment.

events.name: Battle Frontier: boss
events.intro: Round 4, the Brain. A tall woman in white comes down the arena steps without hurrying, and the crowd goes completely silent. Frontier Brain, Lady Imara: "Three rounds is good. Four is the Frontier."

success.text: She raises one hand. Behind her, the board lights up: ROUND 4.
A smile, the first. "Then you'll have it." Her team comes out two levels stronger than it should be. The prize doubles on the board.

win.text: You asked the Frontier Brain for her best, and beat it.

remembers.notice: Second time through: they have heard about you, and they have trained.

success.text: She raises one hand. Behind her, the board lights up: ROUND 4.

events.name: Battle Frontier: exit
events.intro: Daylight, through the arena's high doors. The crowd is still on its feet. Mr. Diallo meets you at the exit with something small and bright on a ribbon. "Symbol's yours."

success.text: The Frontier Symbol is heavier than it looks. Mr. Diallo shakes your hand. "Four rounds. Not many do." Under the Symbol he has tucked a Choice Band, as is Frontier custom.

effects.text: You won the Battle Frontier's Symbol.

success.text: "Again?" Mr. Diallo looks at you over his glasses, and then laughs. "From round one. They'll all be a level sharper." He opens the arena doors again.

events.name: An Exhibition Poster
events.intro: A poster on a lamppost, half torn: "LEAGUE EXHIBITION. TONIGHT. ALL CHALLENGERS WELCOME. NOTHING TO LOSE." Somebody has drawn a little crown on it in pen.

success.text: You follow the arrows on the posters, lamppost after lamppost, to a hall lit up like a festival.
You leave the poster flapping in the wind.

events.name: League Exhibition
events.intro: A hushed hall, its seats full, every face turned to the floor. An usher in white gloves leans down to you. Usher: "Exhibition. Two matches. Nothing to lose, no badge to win. Everyone's watching."

success.text: The usher lifts the rope for you. The quiet in the hall is the loudest thing you have ever walked into.
You slip back out into the night. Inside, the crowd sighs, and settles to wait for someone else.
You stand at the back and watch one match through. The Elite on the floor tonight leads with the same Pokémon every time, and every time, they win with it. You note what it is.

events.name: League Exhibition
events.intro: Match 1. One of the region's Elite Four, off duty, in a cardigan instead of their League colours. "Show me how you'd beat me," they say. "I won't hold it against you. Honestly."

success.text: They smile and send out their lead, the one you saw, or would have.

events.name: League Exhibition: boss
events.intro: Match 2, the Boss. A young man in a Champion's coat that does not quite fit him. "The Champion's busy," says Ferran, the understudy. "I'm what you get. I'm good."

success.text: He squares his shoulders inside the borrowed coat.
"I lost the final," he says. "Twice. Same Champion, both times." He shrugs, and the coat slips. "I'm still here. That counts for something, doesn't it?" It does.

events.name: League Exhibition: exit
events.intro: Daylight, or the hall's bright doors. The crowd is on its feet for you, the whole hall of them, clapping, someone whistling through their fingers.

success.text: You wave, a little awkwardly, and the noise doubles. A child in the front row waves back with both arms. People will remember the challenger who stopped to wave.
You duck out the side door while they are still clapping. Outside the night is cool and quiet. Ferran is out there too, by himself, and gives you a nod.

events.name: Lost Civilization
events.intro: Your ruin rubbings line up, at last, with a coast no map shows. At the end of the jetty a boat waits, as if it has been waiting a long time. In it sits a boatman, silent and old, his hands folded on the oars.

success.text: He rows without a word. The coast drops behind you, and then there is only sea, and then, out of the mist, an island with faces carved into its cliffs.
He holds up ten fingers. Then ten again. Then he puts his hands back on the oars, and looks at you, and waits a little longer.
You leave him at the jetty. He does not seem to mind. He has had practice.

events.name: Lost Island
events.intro: Vines over stone faces, hundreds of them, eyes closed. A stair cut into the cliff. Pots still on a step where someone set them down, a thousand years ago, and never came back for them. A civilization that left in a hurry.

success.text: You climb the stair between the sleeping faces.
You go back down to the boat. The boatman rows you home without a word, as if this too is something he has seen many times.

You trace them with your fingers. They are not gods. They are people: a city of them, carved in the hour it sank. This island was its lookout. They are still looking out to sea, waiting for it to come back up.

events.name: Lost Island
events.intro: The Ruins. Something stirs among the statues: a Bronzor, drifting from face to face, turning slowly, ringing very softly whenever it touches stone.

success.text: It rings once, sharply, and turns its face to you.

You follow the Bronzor at a distance. It drifts along a path you would never have found, round the edge of a courtyard where the tiles are loose and the ground beneath them is hollow. It knows this place.

events.name: Lost Island: trainer
events.intro: The Watcher. Someone is waiting at the top of the stair, arms folded, sunburnt and very serious. Island scholar Tavita: "Nobody comes here. Nobody has for twenty years. Prove you're careful."

success.text: "Careful," she says, "means you don't mind losing."

She takes the rubbings, and goes very still, and reads them twice. "You copied these from the mainland stones. You understood them." She hands them back as if they are made of glass. "Come on. I'll show you the way. I've been waiting for someone who'd understand."

events.name: Lost Island: hidden
events.intro: A Sealed Chamber. A door of black stone, its lock cold and old: a hole in the shape of a bell, and around it, carvings of the sea rising.

success.text: The bell from the Sunken City fits the lock exactly. You ring it once. The sound goes down into the island and comes back up from very far below, and the door swings in. Inside, on a plinth, a sea-green treasure, and a carving of a great shape asleep under the waves.

effects.text: You rang the Sunken City's bell on the Lost Island, and the sealed door opened.

failure.text: The bell fits the lock exactly. You ring it once, and the door swings in. Inside, on a plinth, a red-gold treasure, and a carving of a great shape asleep under the earth.

effects.text: You rang the Sunken City's bell on the Lost Island, and the sealed door opened.

success.text: You put your shoulder to the door until something gives: not the door. You and your lead are bruised for it. Through a crack you see a glint, out of reach.
You leave the chamber sealed. Whatever is behind it has waited this long.

events.name: Lost Island: trap
events.intro: A Trap. A floor of loose stone tiles, each carved with a face. Some faces are worn smooth from walking. Some are clean, as if nobody ever dared step on them.

success.text: You step only on the worn faces, the way the city did. The floor holds. It was never a trap for the people who lived here: they walked on their own faces for luck.
You pick your way between them, and the tiles between the faces drop away under you. Everyone gets a scrape climbing out.

remembers.notice: Tavita stops you with a hand on your arm. "Faces," she says. "Always the faces."
Ahead, the Bronzor you followed drifts over the tiles, touching only the worn faces.

success.text: You step where it hums. The floor never moves. On the far side, the Bronzor rings once, pleased, and drifts away.

events.name: Lost Island: boss
events.intro: The Guardian. The deepest room, a hall open to the sky. In the middle, kneeling, a Golurk as tall as a house: an Alpha, built a thousand years ago to guard the lookout. Its eyes light when you come in. It stands.

success.text: You ring the bell, once, the way the city must have. The Golurk stops. It lowers its great head, and kneels again, and lets you pass. It has been waiting a long time to hear that sound.

effects.text: You calmed the Lost Island's Alpha Golurk with the old city's bell.

success.text: It raises its fists. The hall shakes.

events.name: Lost Island: exit
events.intro: The Exit. Daylight, and the sea far below. And under the water, a shimmer: streets, and roofs, and towers, all drowned and all quite clear. The Sunken City, right where the faces have been looking all along.

success.text: You climb down to the water and slip under.
The boatman is waiting. He looks at the island for a long time, as you row away, as if saying goodbye to someone.

events.name: The Underwater Ruins
events.intro: The Underwater Ruins. Pillars under clear green water, a doorway, a staircase going down to nowhere. Something glints on the bottom between two fallen columns.

success.text: You go down until your ears hurt. It is a crown: a small one, a child's, made for some festival that never came again. Beside it, a pearl. You bring both up into the light.

effects.text: You found a child's crown in the Sunken City.

success.text: You leave the crown where it is. It belongs to the city. You float a while above the drowned streets, and then you swim back up into the sun.
